newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher, but FOMC expected.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher, but FOMC expected.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed higher following word the Federal Open Market Committee left short-term interest rate steady, but anticipation of the decision limited the move, traders said.
Most analysts and traders for weeks had been expecting the Fed to leave monetary policy unchanged at the two-day meeting, and those views were reflected in a 2 1/2-month rally, traders said.
While September Treasury bond futures posted a fresh session high of 112-04 in the final half-hour of trading, the move up was gradual. The contract ended just off the high.

Nearby Eurodollar futures, which have been drifting in a sideways pattern for almost three weeks, showed no price reaction to the Fed move. The December contract posted a two-basis-point range for the entire day.

Floor traders who had hoped that getting the confirmation of steady Fed policy would spark price movement were disappointed. But they emphasized that Thursday's U.S. employment data could stir up volatility.
"Tomorrow is the far more significant event as it turns out," one Eurodollar broker said.
June nonfarm payrolls are seen rising 222,000, compared with a gain of 138,000 in May, and the unemployment rate is seen unchanged at 4.8 percent.
The Eurodollar broker said a weaker than forecast payroll number could send the December contract soaring to 94.12. "The risk is to the upside," he said.
But there is also the possibility that summer employment among students and in the construction industry could inflate the number beyond the average forecast, he said.
The data will arrive on a holiday-shortened trading day. U.S. markets are closed Friday for the July 4th holiday.

Earlier in the day, debt futures had little reaction to U.S. May factory orders data. Orders fell 0.7 percent, versus average trade estimates for down 0.2 percent. The rise in April orders was revised up to 1.4 percent, from 1.2 percent as originally reported.
September T-bonds closed up 12/32 at 112-2/32, December Eurodollars ended up 0.015 at 93.965 and 10-year T-notes ended up 5/32 at 108-14/32. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
